question: What owns table topology, cell coordinates, selection, clipboard and layout?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles maximum-value hard-cut comparison; bounded native subagent source investigations; source-bound public-API probes
trigger: User selected the next ledger item after skipping diff, confirmed table, and said ok go. Assessment and recording are authorized; product execution and publication are outside this request.
requirements: Assess every one of the 14 mapped table census members and materially different consumers, including the React owner omitted from the original scope owner list; keep table independent of other feature reviews.
Preserve rich and non-text content, complete slices, root ownership and atomic rejection through merge, paste, drop and structural edits.
Explicit canonical targets win over current selection; logical row/column coordinates account for merged spans; absent entities and rejected writes produce honest results.
Keep Plite canonical changes, root-aware fitting, selection, history and authored semantics authoritative; Table owns product rectangle/span policy and configurable schema descriptors.
Gesture, caret/selection paint and cleanup honor the exact mounted view; selection caches distinguish authored selections sharing a projection.
Consider keep/configure, changed APIs, missing primitives, delete/merge/inline, ownership moves and architecture replacement; runtime replacement remains provisional until executable comparison.
Reconcile prior decisions, retain proof limits, append immutable review history, and recommend one next owner without changing product code.
evidenceReuse: Initial immutable table review. Re-read current source and consumers rather than importing historical pass claims. June 15 extension-owned grid policy, July staged refactor, August renderer-hook cut and September resize ownership remain context; July name-preservation constraints do not bind this beta review. Fresh 236-test core and 48-test React partitions pass. New source-bound probes reproduce image loss on merge, mixed-slice sibling loss, ignored explicit replacement/insertion targets and a UI-only merge restriction. The authored cache issue is source-traced, not runtime-reproduced. No new external discovery.
summary: Pursue Task design/plan for canonical table edits and complete-content preservation. The strongest cut is the redundant generic TableOperation instruction vocabulary and its detached/transaction/paste interpreters, plus unused transfer provenance and public grid/compiler plumbing. Retain private rectangle/span algorithms, table/row/cell descriptors, headless/React separation and local resize previews. Reproduced data loss and target/policy contradictions independently justify work; the replacement runtime must still beat or match the current complete-operation path under explicit correctness and scale gates.
alternatives: Keep/configure loses: existing switches cannot prevent reproduced image/sibling loss or explicit-target violations. Existing passing suites do not cover these failures.

Change existing APIs: canonical NodeTarget resolution, one domain selection answer, honest absence/rejection, valid construction and owner-enforced merge policy remove caller reconstruction and contradictory behavior. Exact signatures remain for design.

Add primitive only for a demonstrated gap in canonical candidate transactions, complete-slice fitting or exact-view lifetime. No new public table controller, grid store, operation-plan API or generic plugin package.

Delete/merge/inline is the strongest candidate: replace transient generic TableOperation instructions and repeated interpreters with canonical transaction construction and fitters; retain pure table-domain calculations. Delete unused paste-source stack and hide compiler/context/metrics. Runtime adoption is provisional pending measured comparison.

Move ownership: table topology and UX policy stay Plate-owned; Plite remains canonical change/root/rollback owner. Mounted React owns gestures/paint/retirement; copied UI owns menus and visuals. Repair insufficient Plite primitives at their owner instead of product glue.

Replace architecture with a flat spreadsheet model, raw-core table feature or parallel selection/controller loses: nested rich cells, existing schema/codec identities and customizable renderers provide real jobs for the current feature boundary.
Keep the September resize split and automatic row/cell dependencies. Do not reintroduce renderer state bags or merge unrelated Plate features merely to shorten imports.

Delete the orphan selected-cell drag capture/MIME/drop protocol after its trigger was removed. Compare exact-view plugin element attributes against the exported selection DOM hook, preserving caret/DOM/native laws under a benchmark gate. Keep real row DnD and the existing resize lifecycle.
proofLimits: Assessment only; no product repairs, type/declaration closure, current browser/device run, extreme-span stress or candidate benchmark. Existing core partition: 236 pass across 19 files, 19067 assertions. React partition: 48 pass across 5 files, 200 assertions. The retained probe is an observation script, not a test asserting broken behavior as desired. Authored-view cache contamination and import-work/rowgroup concerns are source-derived, not runtime-reproduced. Existing preparation-only benchmarks cannot accept the replacement; require complete fitting/publication, rollback, rich/named-root content, history, multi-view authored selection and scale comparison. Global inventory check has an unrelated pre-existing stale AI observation; table record freshness is validated separately. The September resize plan retains a failed native selection-paint positive control on baseline and candidate; it is not closed by the historical resize passes. Same-row and multirow handle behavior differ in current browser assertions.
